newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks higher at start of weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks higher at start of weekly trade.

text.p: Jordanian stocks rose at the start of weekly trade on Saturday underpinned by leading Arab Bank Ltd, a key component of the official index, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 1.26 percent to 144.34 points from 142.54 points on Wednesday.
Dealers said market sentiment was buttressed by Arab Bank and a few blue-chip firms heavily weighted in the official 60-share index, such as Arab Potash Company.
The exchange's weakness sent the index below 140 points at the end of June, sliding to levels not reached since 1993.

A total of 398,355 shares changed hands on Wednesday in a moderate 596,520 dinar turnover in the cash-squeezed market. Of 46 stocks traded, 24 advanced, 13 fell and nine were unchanged. Three posted year lows.
"Generally stocks have improved but the volume is small and the companies that are influential in the index have pushed up the market in improved sentiment," one broker said.

Investor sentiment, dampened after recent unrest fueled by the government's doubling of bread prices in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms, was boosted after Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti pledged to encourage private sector investment, dealers said.

Investors say the 44 million dinar capitalised Arab Bank, the kingdom's leading bank, is a main beneficiary of a new draft companies law which would cancel a 15 percent tax levied on capital increases. Its management has promised to distribute a bonus share to its shareholders once the tax is cancelled.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- firmed 0.31 percent to 80.02 points. It was 15.17 percent down on last year.

In industrials, the leading sector, Jordan Cement Factories rose 20 fils to 3.390 dinars with a few dealers citing some limited foreign buying on the stock which the government plans to sell part of its majority stake. Livestock and Poultry rose 20 fils to 570 fils on a large 125,023 dinar turnover. Arab Potash Company climbed on reports of boosted potash exports, the country's main hard currency earner, in the first half of 1996.
In services, Jordan Electric Power rose 10 fils to 1.540 dinars and National Portfolio also firmed 10 fils to 1.200 dinars.
In banks, trading was generally thin, with Arab Bank's 2.50 dinars rise to 231.500 dinars supporting the market. Islamic Bank rose 20 fils to 3.580 dinars on a a minimal 20,174 dinars turnover.

Industrials dominated, with a 274,274 dinar turnover and an index rise of 2.09 percent, services had a 100,915 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.31 percent while banks had a low 97,981 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.78 percent.
A total of 124,377 shares worth 79,805 dinars changed hands in thin trade in the parallel market with Industrial Ceramics and Arab Financial Investment dominating trade.
